raw_response:
I’m 65 now, and on 9 mu I can’t afford to gamble too much. I mostly follow what has worked on my land and what the other farmers nearby do. Wheat and maize are still my main way to keep the land busy and bring in steady grain, but I also keep some cotton because I’ve grown it many years and if grain price is not good, cotton can still bring some cash. Since some people in my family work outside, I can’t make the field work too complicated. I will keep fertilizer and water at a middle level, not the highest, because pumping water costs money and too much fertilizer also costs cash. For wheat, I’ll put base fertilizer before sowing and then topdress once in spring. For maize, I’ll plant right after wheat harvest so I don’t lose time, and I’ll give it one base dose and one topdress when it grows fast. Cotton I’ll keep on a smaller piece, manage more carefully, and spray only if pests show up badly. I do things the steady way, not chasing the biggest yield, just trying to avoid a bad year.
